No. The 2022 loss was not detected with Sentinel-2. It was mapped by Hansen/UMD Global Forest Change (GFC-2025-v1.13), which uses 30 m pixels and an annual series from 2001 to 2025. The evidence shows about 0.6 ha of tree-cover loss in 2022, or 3.41% of the 17.6 ha asset.

Sentinel-2 does not appear among the sources. The JRC GFC2020 reference map is 10 m, but it is a forest/non-forest map for 2020, not the detection source. The JRC map agrees with the event area (fraction 1.0), and a later year (up to 2025) was observed, so the loss is corroborated under the method.

The evidence does not establish deforestation or land-use change, the cause, legality, responsibility, or any compliance finding.
